title: Flash Memory vs RAM Power Cycle
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: Robotics and Computational Thinking
description: Save main.py, run it, change a variable, and cut the power to see that Flash memory keeps your files while RAM forgets everything.

educational.topic: Non-volatile flash storage versus volatile RAM on a microcontroller
learningObjectives: Explain that Flash memory keeps saved files when power is removed
Explain that RAM holds running variables only while the board has power
Predict the value of a variable after a power cycle
Explain why large files do not fit in 2 MB of flash storage
prerequisites: Flash memory stores programs on the board (Chapter 2: Storing Your Programs)
A variable is a named value a program uses and can change

controls.label: Save main.py to Flash
controls.purpose: Store main.py (1 KB) in flash; becomes Saved

controls.label: Run program
controls.purpose: Put speed = 50 and distance_cm = 32 in RAM

controls.label: Change speed to 80
controls.purpose: Change the variable in RAM only

controls.label: Power OFF / Power ON
controls.purpose: Cut or restore power; power on re-runs main.py

controls.label: Add a 2 MB picture file
controls.purpose: Try to save a file that is too large

simulationModel.modelType: Discrete state machine of a microcontroller's memory
assumptions: main.py sets speed = 50 and distance_cm = 32 when it starts
The board runs main.py automatically at power-on
MicroPython uses 640 KB of the 2048 KB flash, leaving 1408 KB for files
limitations: Real RAM also holds the MicroPython interpreter and other objects
Files can be written to flash from a running program; this model does not show that

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Predict-observe-explain with a step-through state machine
pedagogical.interactionPattern: One button per action with a plain-sentence log
keyQuestions: After you change speed to 80 and cycle the power, what is speed?
Which memory kept main.py when the power was off?
Why does the board run main.py again when the power comes back?
Why can a 2 MB picture not be saved on the board?
commonMisconceptions: Changing a variable while the program runs also changes the saved file
Turning the power off erases the saved program
The board's full 2 MB is free for your own files
assessmentOpportunities: Written prediction of speed after a power cycle
Challenge: speed returns to 50 and Flash kept main.py
Exit ticket naming one Flash item and one RAM item
